hazards.evidence: Everyday dishes/bowls stacked on the lowest shelf near floor level on the right-hand open shelving, requiring deep bending (hip-precaution risk) while using a walker.
Stacks of frequently used bowls/dishes kept on the upper open shelf at about shoulder height on the right shelving unit; reaching high while on a walker can cause loss of balance.
A wooden chair is sitting in the central kitchen walkway in front of the sink/dishwasher, narrowing and obstructing the walker path.
Freestanding wooden chair (no arms, not load-rated as a support) placed by the counter/sink where it may be grabbed or used for reaching/support.
Smooth, glossy vinyl/tile floor in front of the sink and stove shows a reflective sheen, indicating a potentially slippery surface when wet.
Floor surface changes from kitchen tile to carpet at the right-side doorway with no contrasting edge marking, a possible trip/level-transition point for a walker.
